items.from: A: The Bitter Struggle authors (Ben Buchanan, Tantum Collins)
items.to: 1 Export controls on advanced chips to China
items.capacity: Ben Buchanan, co-author; former White House AI adviser; interviewed by ChinaTalk
items.fact: In a January 2026 interview, Buchanan said a blanket FDPR ban on chipmaking equipment for China would have been more aggressive than the Dutch and Japanese negotiations.
items.quote: the more aggressive option would have been using the FDPR to essentially blanket ban
items.missing: Book text and any 2025-2026 essay on chip export controls not found; the Foreign Affairs essay is paywalled.
items.notes: Retrospective on Biden-era decisions. Byline says 'Ben Buchanan, now at SAIS'.

items.to: 1 Export controls on advanced chips to China
items.capacity: Anthropic, company policy submission on the Commerce AI diffusion rule
items.fact: Anthropic said in April 2025 that maintaining US compute advantage through chip export controls is essential for national security.
items.quote: maintaining America's compute advantage through export controls is essential for national security and economic prosperity
items.notes: Anthropic's Feb 26, 2026 statement says it has 'advocated for strong export controls on chips to ensure a democratic advantage' (page read).

items.from: A: The Bitter Struggle authors (Ben Buchanan, Tantum Collins)
items.to: 2 Democracies or the US and allies holding the lead in frontier AI
items.capacity: Penguin Random House book description for The Bitter Struggle (Buchanan and Collins); publisher text, not an author's own words
items.fact: The book's publisher description says the US and its democratic allies must not lose the AI contest.
items.quote: the United States and its democratic allies must not lose this contest
items.missing: Authors' own essays or interviews on the lead question not found in searches.
items.notes: Penguin RH page lists 'Published on Nov 10, 2026'.

items.to: 2 Democracies or the US and allies holding the lead in frontier AI
items.capacity: Anthropic, company policy submission on the Commerce AI diffusion rule
items.fact: Anthropic said in April 2025 that the US still maintains a lead in AI development, though Chinese labs have made significant progress.
items.quote: While the U.S. still maintains a lead in AI development
items.notes: Anthropic's Feb 26, 2026 statement says 'using AI to defend the United States and other democracies' (page read). Page is tagged 'Democratic lead'.

items.to: 2 Democracies or the US and allies holding the lead in frontier AI
items.capacity: Author of the UK AI Opportunities Action Plan (UK government publication); former Prime Minister's AI adviser
items.fact: The UK plan says the UK must lead in both building and using AI to remain a world leader.
items.quote: to remain a world leader we need to lead in both building and using AI
items.missing: No democracies-as-a-bloc position in the plan text read; 'key allies' appears only in a compute-access context.
items.notes: UK-specific claim, not a position on democracies collectively. Plan also says the UK should be 'the best state partner to those building frontier AI'. Publication day not read; brief gives January 2025.

items.from: A: The Bitter Struggle authors (Ben Buchanan, Tantum Collins)
items.to: 3 Governments adopting frontier AI in public services and national security
items.capacity: Penguin Random House book description for The Bitter Struggle (Buchanan and Collins); publisher text, not an author's own words
items.fact: The book's publisher description says democracies must deploy AI without surrendering their values, and that so far they are failing.
items.quote: Democracies must also deploy AI’s capabilities without surrendering their own values
items.missing: Authors' own statements on public-sector adoption not found in searches.
items.notes: Foreign Affairs essay 'The AI Grand Bargain' (Nov/Dec 2025) found in search, paywalled and not read; search excerpt says it proposes a deal between tech companies and the federal government.

items.to: 3 Governments adopting frontier AI in public services and national security
items.capacity: Dario Amodei, Anthropic CEO, company statement on discussions with the Department of War
items.fact: Anthropic said on February 26, 2026 that Claude is extensively deployed in US national security agencies for mission-critical work.
items.quote: Claude is extensively deployed across the Department of War and other national security agencies
items.missing: Civilian public-service adoption (Claude for Government) seen in search summaries only, not read.
items.notes: Same statement says 'We were the first frontier AI company to deploy our models in the US government's classified networks'. Later Pentagon dispute reported in secondary sources only.

items.to: 3 Governments adopting frontier AI in public services and national security
items.capacity: Author of the UK AI Opportunities Action Plan; former Prime Minister's AI adviser
items.fact: The UK plan says the public sector should rapidly pilot and scale AI products and services to improve outcomes and productivity.
items.quote: The public sector should rapidly pilot and scale AI products and services
items.missing: No Clifford statement on national-security adoption found; the plan is the only source read on this point.
items.notes: Recommendation sits under 'Push hard on cross-economy AI adoption' (Section 2). A 'Scan, Pilot, Scale' label from a search summary was not verified on the page and is not used.

items.capacity: Ben Buchanan and Tantum Collins (no statement found)
items.fact: No dated Buchanan or Collins statement on safety or security institutes testing frontier models was found.
items.missing: Foreign Affairs essay 'The AI Grand Bargain' not read (paywalled); no interview or essay on institute testing surfaced.
items.notes: Searched 'Ben Buchanan AI Safety Institute frontier model testing pre-deployment evaluation views'; it returned institute and CAISI background only. The book description (read) names no testing institute.

items.to: 4 State safety or security institutes testing frontier models
items.capacity: Anthropic, company post on safeguards collaboration with US CAISI and UK AISI
items.fact: Anthropic said in September 2025 that CAISI and UK AISI teams had access to its systems at several development stages for ongoing testing.
items.quote: allowing for ongoing testing of our systems
items.missing: Anthropic's original 2024 CAISI agreement text not read.
items.notes: Post says each body evaluated several Constitutional Classifiers iterations on Claude Opus 4 and 4.1 before deployment. CIO (May 6, 2026, reported) says Anthropic and OpenAI signed similar agreements 'almost two years ago'.

items.to: 4 State safety or security institutes testing frontier models
items.capacity: Author of the UK AI Opportunities Action Plan; former Prime Minister's AI adviser
items.fact: The UK plan recommends continuing to grow the AI Safety Institute, which it says was first to run pre-deployment evaluations of frontier models.
items.quote: AISI is the first safety institute to have conducted pre-deployment evaluations of frontier models
items.missing: Clifford's own statements on testing regimes beyond the plan not found.
items.notes: Recommendation 23 in the plan. Search results say the body was later renamed the AI Security Institute; not verified on a page.

items.from: A: The Bitter Struggle authors (Ben Buchanan, Tantum Collins)
items.to: 5 Building national compute and energy for AI
items.capacity: Ben Buchanan and Tantum Collins (no statement found)
items.fact: No Buchanan or Collins position on building national compute or energy was found; the book description names US data centers only as subject matter.
items.missing: Foreign Affairs essay 'The AI Grand Bargain' not read (paywalled); no 2025-2026 compute or energy policy statement surfaced.
items.notes: Searched 'AI Grand Bargain Buchanan Collins Foreign Affairs' (search excerpts only). The publisher text mentions 'city-sized data centers in America' as subject matter; not treated as a position.

items.to: 5 Building national compute and energy for AI
items.capacity: Anthropic, company policy report 'Build AI in America'
items.fact: Anthropic said in July 2025 that US AI leadership requires substantial investment in computing power and electricity.
items.quote: we must make substantial investments in computing power and electricity
items.notes: Report projects 2GW and 5GW data centers for single Anthropic models in 2027 and 2028, and 20-25GW total US frontier training by 2028. A Feb 2026 electricity-cost pledge is in search results only, not read.

items.to: 5 Building national compute and energy for AI
items.capacity: Author of the UK AI Opportunities Action Plan; former Prime Minister's AI adviser
items.fact: The UK plan says government must secure enough compute, expand public AI research compute at least 20x by 2030, and create AI Growth Zones for data centres.
items.quote: The government must therefore secure access to a sufficient supply of compute
items.missing: Clifford's own statements after 2025 on compute or energy not found; plan text read only.
items.notes: Plan says the AI Research Resource should expand 'by at least 20x by 2030'; AI Growth Zones are to 'facilitate the accelerated build out of AI data centres'. Plan says sovereign compute will be the smallest component of UK compute.

items.from: A: The Bitter Struggle authors (Ben Buchanan, Tantum Collins)
items.to: 6 How soon very powerful AI arrives
items.capacity: Penguin Random House book description for The Bitter Struggle (Buchanan and Collins); publisher text, not an author's own words
items.fact: The book's publisher description says the next few years may decide the next few decades, without naming an arrival date.
items.quote: why the next few years may decide the next few decades
items.missing: No author-stated arrival date found in the description or searches.
items.notes: Weak signal: a stakes framing, not a timeline. The same description says AI progress has been 'so stunning and yet so predictable'.

items.to: 6 How soon very powerful AI arrives
items.capacity: Dario Amodei, Anthropic CEO, personal essay
items.fact: In a January 2026 essay, Amodei wrote that powerful AI could be as little as one to two years away, though possibly much further out.
items.quote: powerful AI could be as little as 1–2 years away
items.notes: Essay date (26 Jan 2026) comes from secondary coverage; the page was read by text search only. The essay also refers to a 'country of geniuses' materializing in ~2027. Earlier: Oct 2024 'Machines of Loving Grace' says 'I think it could come as early as 2026'.

items.to: 6 How soon very powerful AI arrives
items.capacity: Matt Clifford, keynote at RBC Capital Markets UK Focus Conference (as reported by RBC)
items.fact: Per RBC's report of his keynote, Clifford said the real AI disruption has not truly begun.
items.quote: the real disruption hasn't truly begun
items.missing: Clifford's own transcript or slides not read; the timing claim is RBC's paraphrase.
items.notes: 'Why 2026 may be the last normal year' is RBC's headline, not Clifford's words. RBC byline lists conflicting titles (ARIA chair; AI Safety Institute vice chair). His 2023 'two years' remark is disputed and not used.
